hints: Recall the principle of conservation of linear momentum: total initial momentum equals total final momentum along the line of motion.
Set up the momentum balance equation: $m(5) + 0.3(0) = m(2) + 0.3v$.
Subtract $2m$ from both sides to get $0.3v = 3m$, then divide by 0.3 to express $v$ in terms of $m$.
walkthrough:
Name the foundational principle: in the absence of external horizontal forces on a smooth plane, linear momentum is conserved in the collision:
$$m_P u_P + m_Q u_Q = m_P v_P + m_Q v_Q$$

List the known values for both particles along the line of motion:
$$m_P = m\text{ kg},\quad u_P = 5\text{ m s}^{-1},\quad v_P = 2\text{ m s}^{-1}$$
$$m_Q = 0.3\text{ kg},\quad u_Q = 0\text{ m s}^{-1}$$

Substitute these quantities into the momentum conservation equation:
$$m(5) + (0.3)(0) = m(2) + (0.3)v$$
$$5m = 2m + 0.3v$$

Subtract $2m$ from both sides of the equation:
$$5m - 2m = 0.3v$$
$$3m = 0.3v$$

Divide both sides by $0.3$ to express the speed of $Q$ in terms of $m$:
$$v = \frac{3m}{0.3} = \frac{30m}{3} = 10m\text{ m s}^{-1}$$

hints: Apply conservation of linear momentum to the collision between $Q$ and $R$.
Substitute the initial speed of $Q$ as $10m$, noting that $Q$ comes to rest and $R$ moves off at $1.5\text{ m s}^{-1}$.
Solve the resulting equation $3m = 0.9$ to determine the mass $m$.
walkthrough:
Name the principle of conservation of linear momentum for the collision between particles $Q$ and $R$:
$$m_Q u_Q + m_R u_R = m_Q v_Q + m_R v_R$$

List all parameters for this second impact:
$$m_Q = 0.3\text{ kg},\quad u_Q = 10m\text{ m s}^{-1},\quad v_Q = 0\text{ m s}^{-1}$$
$$m_R = 0.6\text{ kg},\quad u_R = 0\text{ m s}^{-1},\quad v_R = 1.5\text{ m s}^{-1}$$

Substitute these values into the conservation of momentum equation:
$$(0.3)(10m) + (0.6)(0) = (0.3)(0) + (0.6)(1.5)$$

Divide both sides by 3 to find $m$:
$$m = \frac{0.9}{3} = 0.3\text{ kg}$$
